title: Reach the date with a keyboard
goal: A customer who uses only the keyboard books the 09:00 slot on a chosen date, and the booking is saved and reopens with that exact date.

steps.headline: Keyboard user got stuck at the date step: there is no date field to Tab to

steps.diagnosis: The date picker element is a div that cannot receive keyboard focus, preventing keyboard-only users from entering a date. Changing it to a focusable input allows tabbing and typing the date.

steps.reasoning:
We need to diagnose why keyboard booking fails. Evidence: focus trail shows after selecting provider, next button clicked, but then page shows timezone select and calendar but no date field? Actually verifier expects date field with id "select-date" or "native-date". In booking.js, $selectDate = $('#select-date'); That's a div. The datepicker is initialized on that div. However, the verifier says after step 2, they wait for date field with id "select-date" (or "native-date"), Tab to it, press Control+A, type date, Enter, then Tab. But maybe the datepicker is not focusable because it's a div without tabindex. Keyboard users cannot focus a div unless it's made focusable. The verifier likely fails to focus the datepicker, so they cannot type date. Thus we need to make the date picker input focusable. Perhaps we should change the div to an input type="text" or add tabindex="0". But we cannot change HTML directly? We can edit booking_time_step.php where the div is defined. Change
to or add tabindex="0". Simpler: add tabindex="0". Let's edit booking_time_step.php. Also need to ensure that after typing date and pressing Enter, the datepicker accepts. The datepicker likely works on div; but if we make it focusable, keyboard events may still work. Let's propose edit: change line to include tabindex="0". Also maybe add role="application"? Not needed. Check if any other issue: After date selection, they need to see 09:00 slot. That depends on getAvailableHours being called on date change. The datepicker's onChange triggers getAvailableHours. If we manually type date and press Enter, does it trigger change? The datepicker likely updates via its own mechanism; but if we simulate typing, maybe not. Better to keep the datepicker as is and just make it focusable so that when tabbed, the datepicker widget opens and user can navigate with arrow keys. The verifier wants to type date directly; but maybe they expect typing works because it's an input type=text with datepicker attached. Currently it's a div; typing does nothing. So we need to change to input. Let's change to . The datepicker likely works on input. We'll edit booking_time_step.php. Now need to verify that this doesn't break pointer users. Input should still work. Let's craft proposal.

steps.diagnosis: The date picker is inline, causing the month to change when the user types a date in a different month, which triggers the onMonthChange handler and overrides the user's input with the first available date of the month. Changing the date picker to non-inline prevents the month change during typing, so the onMonthChange handler is not triggered and the user's input is preserved.

steps.reasoning:
We are given that the verifier attempted to type a date (02/11/2026) but the page changed it back to 01/11/2026.
 Looking at the evidence, we see:
   After typing the date, the page made a request for get_available_hours and then get_unavailable_dates.
   Then, the page code set the date field to "01/11/2026" via setDate in applyUnavailableDates.

 The problem is that when the user types a date, the date picker's onChange handler triggers getAvailableHours and updateConfirmFrame.
 Then, because of the month change (if the typed date is in a different month than the currently displayed month), the onMonthChange handler is triggered.
 In onMonthChange, we call getUnavailableDates, which in turn calls applyUnavailableDates with setDate=true.
 In applyUnavailableDates, we set the date to the first available date in the month (which might be the first day of the month if the user typed a date that is unavailable).

 However, note that the verifier typed a date that is available (02/11/2026) but the page set it to 01/11/2026.

 Let's look at the applyUnavailableDates function in booking_http_client.js:

   if (setDate && !vars('manage_mode')) {
        for (let i = 1; i <= numberOfDays; i++) {
            const currentDate = new Date(selectedDate.getFullYear(), selectedDate.getMonth(), i);

            if (unavailableDates.indexOf(moment(currentDate).format('YYYY-MM-DD')) === -1) {
                App.Utils.UI.setDateTimePickerValue($selectDate, currentDate);
                getAvailableHours(moment(currentDate).format('YYYY-MM-DD'));
                break;
            }
        }
   }

 This loop sets the date to the first available day in the month. The verifier typed the 2nd, but the first day (1st) was available, so it set to the 1st.

 We want to preserve the user's typed date if it is available. The current code overrides it.

 We should change the logic: if the user has typed a date (and it is available) we should not override it.

 However, note that the verifier is in the process of typing the date and then pressing Enter. The date field is updated by the user's input.

 The problem is that the onMonthChange handler is triggered when the month changes (because the flatpickr instance updates the displayed month when the user types a date that is in a different month?).

   After typing: date_field_value becomes "02/11/2026"
   Then, after the getUnavailableDates request, the page sets it to "01/11/2026"

 Let me check the flatpickr options: we have onChange and onMonthChange.

 The onChange fires when the date is changed. The onMonthChange fires when the month is changed.

 The verifier typed the date in the same month, so onMonthChange should not fire.

 The onMonthChange is triggered when the month is changed in the date picker. But note: the verifier typed the date, which does not change the month displayed in the calendar? Unless the calendar was showing October and the user typed November.

We prevent this override when the date picker is not inline (i.e., a popup) by checking the inline configuration before auto-setting the date.

steps.reasoning:
We need to understand why the typed date is being overridden. The evidence shows that after typing "02/11/2026", the page code sets the date field to "01/11/2026" via setDate ← setDateTimePickerValue ← applyUnavailableDates ← ... ← onMonthChange ← setDate.

So even though we made the date picker non-inline, the onMonthChange handler is still being triggered? Actually, the onMonthChange handler is called when the month changes in the date picker. If the date picker is non-inline (i.e., a popup), typing a date might not change the month until the popup closes? But the evidence shows that after typing, the page request for get_unavailable_dates is triggered by onMonthChange. That suggests that the month change is happening even with non-inline? Let's think: flatpickr's onMonthChange is triggered when the displayed month changes, which can happen when the user navigates months via the dropdown or arrows, but also when the date is set programmatically? However, the user typed a date in a different month (they typed 02/11/2026 while the current displayed month is October 2026? Actually, the initial date is set to today (26/10/2026). They typed 02/11/2026, which is November. So the month changed from October to November. The date picker likely updates the displayed month when the date is changed, triggering onMonthChange.

Thus, making it non-inline doesn't prevent the month change when the date is changed. We need to prevent the onMonthChange handler from overriding the user's input when the user has just typed a date. Perhaps we can ignore the setDate call in applyUnavailableDates when the user has just interacted? Or we can avoid calling setDate in applyUnavailableDates when the date is already set by user input? Look at the applyUnavailableDates function: it has a condition `if (setDate && !vars('manage_mode')) { ... }`. That block sets the date to the first available date in the month if the current date is unavailable? Actually, it loops through days to find the first enabled date and sets it. That is what is overriding the user's input: after getting unavailable dates, it sets the date to the first available date (which is 01/11/2026) because the user typed 02/11/2026 but maybe that date is unavailable? Wait, the user wants 09:00 slot on 02/11/2026. The evidence shows that after typing the date, the page requests get_available_hours (which would return slots for that date). Then it requests get_unavailable_dates (maybe due to onMonthChange). Then applyUnavailableDates sets the date to the first available date in the month (01/11/2026). That suggests that the get_unavailable_dates request is being triggered incorrectly.

Why is get_unavailable_dates being called? Because onMonthChange is triggered when the month changes. The onMonthChange handler calls getUnavailableDates. That is happening after the user types the date and the date picker updates the month. We need to prevent the onMonthChange handler from running when the change is due to user input? Or we need to make sure that after the user types a date, we don't want to fetch unavailable dates for the new month? Actually, the purpose of onMonthChange is to preload unavailable dates for the new month when the user navigates months via the dropdown. But when the user types a date, we already have the date and we have fetched available hours for that date. We don't need to fetch unavailable dates for the month.

One solution: disable the onMonthChange handler when the date picker is not inline? But the date picker is now non-inline, but the month still changes when the date is changed. Alternatively, we can modify the onMonthChange handler to not call getUnavailableDates if the date picker is opened? Hmm.

Another approach: In applyUnavailableDates, we should not override the date if the user has just entered it. We can check if the date was set by user input recently? Or we can avoid calling setDate in applyUnavailableDates when the date is already valid (i.e., when the selected date is not in the unavailableDates list). Actually, the applyUnavailableDates function is supposed to grey out unavailable dates and optionally set the date to the first available date. It does that only if setDate is true and not manage mode. The setDate flag is passed as true from getUnavailableDates. We could change the call to applyUnavailableDates in getUnavailableDates to pass false for setDate when the call is triggered by onMonthChange? But we need to differentiate.

Alternatively, we can change the onMonthChange handler to not call getUnavailableDates at all, and instead rely on the date picker's built-in disabling? But the application needs to know unavailable dates to grey them out.

Look at the date picker initialization: it has onChange and onMonthChange and onYearChange. The onChange handler calls getAvailableHours and updateConfirmFrame. That's fine. The onMonthChange and onYearChange handlers call getUnavailableDates to preload unavailable dates for the new month.

Maybe we can change the onMonthHandler to only call getUnavailableDates if the date picker is inline? Because when inline, the month change is visible and we want to preload. When non-inline, the month change happens only when the popup opens? Actually, when non-inline, the date picker is an input that opens a popup when clicked. The month change inside the popup does not affect the underlying input until a date is selected. So perhaps we should keep inline for the date picker to work correctly with keyboard? But the problem is that inline causes the month to change when the date is changed, triggering onMonthChange.

Wait, the date picker is a flatpickr instance. When inline:true, the calendar is always visible. When the user types a date in the input? Actually, if it's inline, there is no input? The original code had a div #select-date and flatpickr was attached to that div, making an inline calendar. There is no input for the user to type. That's why attempt 1 changed it to an in…
